purpose: This policy applies when <<LAB_NAME>> performs mixed lymphocyte culture (MLC) testing for transplant compatibility. Required by 42 CFR 493.1278 (Standard: Histocompatibility).

cfr_text_blocks.label: Standard: Histocompatibility
cfr_text_blocks.verbatim: (a) General. The laboratory must meet the following requirements: (1) Use a continuous monitoring system and alert system to monitor the storage temperature of specimens (donor and recipient) and reagents and notify laboratory personnel when temperature limits are exceeded. (2) Establish and follow written policies and procedures for the storage and retention of specimens based on the specific type of specimen. All specimens must be easily retrievable. The laboratory must have an emergency plan for alternate storage. (3) If the laboratory uses immunologic reagents to facilitate or enhance the isolation or identification of lymphocytes or lymphocyte subsets, the efficacy of the methods must be monitored with appropriate quality control procedures. (4) Participate in at least one national or regional cell exchange program, if available, or develop an exchange system with another laboratory in order to validate interlaboratory reproducibility.

scope: Applies only when <<LAB_NAME>> performs histocompatibility MLC. Personnel and the medical director or designee.
policy_statements: MLC testing is performed per the validated procedure with documented technologist competency.
Controls (positive responder, negative responder, autologous control) are run on each MLC plate per the lab's procedure.
Results are interpreted by qualified personnel per the procedure's interpretation criteria; reported with stimulation index and reference range.
procedure_steps: Set up MLC per the validated procedure with required controls.
Read at the procedure-defined time points; calculate stimulation index.
Interpret per the criteria; report with appropriate clinical comment.
definitions: Test of in vitro lymphocyte proliferation when responder and stimulator cells are co-cultured. Used in transplant compatibility assessment.
